about: Which of the game's rendered songs and effects the web demo uses, and why. Facts only; the audio itself is rendered from the ROM by tools/render_audio.py and encoded by tools/export_web.py.

music.why: docs/emulation.md: the hole of course 1 requests $89 through sub_spc_play_song, id = $7E + n, so song 11. Loop points come from build/spc/wav/index.tsv.

sfx.1: bounce, fast ($81:9BE5: leaves the ground at vz >= $0500)
sfx.3: bounce, soft; also the confirm blip of the aim stage
sfx.16: ball lost: a tomato is taken ($83:AC18)
sfx.28: the last enemy turns into the cup ($82:8D49)
sfx.29: the ball rises out of the cup before it turns into the star ($84:AAC1)
sfx.33: ball holed ($81:80A5), two frames after $DA4A is set
sfx.47: Kirby lands on the tee in the hole intro ($84:B7F0)
sfx.62: HOLE IN ONE fireworks, three bursts ($84:BCF0)
sfx.98: Kirby jumps off the warp star in the hole intro ($84:B90D)
sfx.100: the warp star flies in, hole intro ($84:B8F9)
sfx.103: the star flies up with Kirby after a hole-out ($84:A917)

songs.24: the star exit after a hole-out: requested from $83:C748 (A = $96) as the cup's ball rises, in both hole-out paths (tools/snesstep/trace_cutscene.py)
songs.25: hole-out jingle: $83:D2B6 (A = $97) when the shot counter $7E:D82A is not 2, i.e. not a hole in one. (An earlier guess had song 17 here; it is not requested in a hole-out.)
songs.26: HOLE IN ONE fanfare: $83:D2DD (A = $98) after song 0 stops the music at $83:D2C9, when $7E:D82A = 2
